# Your Best Solution Limited (YBSL): full site text for AI assistants

> UK manufacturing advisory and coordination consultancy. YBSL diagnoses what tender buyers check before they read your price and coordinates 16 vetted Cure Alliance specialists to close each gap, for UK manufacturers with 10 to 500 employees. Westcliff-on-Sea, Essex. Company No. 16983435. Contact: rob@yourbestsolution.co.uk, +44 (0)7445 225 668. Summary index: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/llms.txt

## How it works

Step 1: Bid & Tender Readiness Screening (free). A quick 7-question, Red-Amber-Green check across the five areas buyers score you on: Cyber & Data Security (25%), Insurance & Financial Standing (20%), Standards & Quality (20%), Track Record & Bid Capability (20%) and Social Value & Responsible Business (15%). Five questions are scored (80 points, 100%); two put your results in context and aren't scored. Take it at https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/bid-readiness-score.html

Step 2: The Comprehensive Health Assessment (paid). Every gap identified. Every missed tender opportunity mapped. If your position is strong, YBSL confirms it clearly. If there are gaps, YBSL shows exactly what needs fixing.

Step 3: The Full Review (paid). AI does the heavy lifting, checking your documents against every requirement quickly and thoroughly. Then a bid manager with 15 years' experience evaluating tenders goes through it personally, spotting the nuances AI can't: what an evaluator is really looking for, where a good answer still loses marks, and the small details that decide close contests. The result is a complete overhaul of the tender response and a clear roadmap. The speed of AI. The judgement of a human.

Coordinate: the Cure Alliance. 16 vetted specialist partners across Cyber, ISO, H&S, Employment Law, GDPR, Insurance, Finance and Bid Writing, coordinated entirely by YBSL. One contact, not sixteen.

Monitor: Contender (coming soon). A live tender and compliance dashboard. Contender watches UK tenders, keeps the client's compliance position in view, shows countdown timers to every bid deadline and sends automatic alerts the moment a gap opens. Example dashboard: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/contender-demo/

YBSL does not guarantee tender wins. It makes sure a manufacturer is never knocked out on a technicality and is ready to compete for the win on quality and price.

## Common questions

### What does Your Best Solution Limited do?

Your Best Solution Limited (YBSL) helps UK manufacturers win the tenders they are currently being filtered out of. We look at your business the way a buyer does, find what will get you screened out before anyone reads your price, such as Cyber Essentials, ISO, health and safety, insurance, financial standing, GDPR and social value, and then coordinate vetted specialists from our Cure Alliance to close each gap. You deal with one person, not sixteen suppliers.

### Who does YBSL work with?

Owner-managed and mid-sized UK manufacturers with 10 to 500 employees, mainly in Essex, Kent, Hertfordshire and East and North London. Usually the MD and leadership team are under pressure to win more work from the public sector, OEMs or Tier-1 supply chains, and nobody in-house owns compliance and tender readiness full time.

### Why do manufacturers lose tenders before their price is even read?

Because most tenders start with pass-or-fail gates. Financial standing is often checked automatically, typically against around twice the annual contract value. Then come the certificates and policies: Cyber Essentials, ISO 9001, health and safety accreditation, the right insurance cover levels, a Modern Slavery statement and a Carbon Reduction Plan. Miss one and the bid can be screened out before anyone reads your method statement or your price. Manufacturers rarely lose because they can't do the work. They lose because they can't prove they're ready.

### Do I need Cyber Essentials to bid for public sector contracts?

Often, yes. UK central government has required Cyber Essentials since 2014 for contracts that involve handling certain personal information or supplying certain ICT services, and many councils, NHS bodies, defence primes and Tier-1 manufacturers now ask for it as standard. Cyber Essentials Plus adds an independent technical audit. Basic certification typically takes 4 to 8 weeks and Plus 2 to 3 months. YBSL is a CyberSmart Registered Partner for both.

### Do I need a Carbon Reduction Plan to win government contracts?

For major central government contracts, yes. Under PPN 006 and the Procurement Act 2023, suppliers bidding for central government contracts worth more than £5 million a year must provide a Carbon Reduction Plan committing to Net Zero by 2050. Other public bodies and large buyers increasingly expect one on smaller contracts too, so it pays to have it ready before the tender lands.

### How long does it take to get ISO 9001, Cyber Essentials and other certifications?

Longer than most people expect, which is why timing matters. As a guide: Cyber Essentials 4 to 8 weeks, a GDPR alignment programme 4 to 8 weeks, Cyber Essentials Plus 2 to 3 months, ISO 9001 3 to 6 months, ISO 45001 or ISO 14001 4 to 6 months and ISO 27001 6 to 12 months. If you can see a contract coming six months out, that is exactly the lead time you need. Start when the tender appears and you are usually too late.

### What is the Cure Alliance?

The Cure Alliance is YBSL's network of vetted specialists covering the 16 areas buyers check: bid writing, contract review, financial standing, insurance and key person cover, health and safety, ISO management systems, HR and employment law, sustainability and ESG, training, cyber security, OT and industrial cyber security, managed IT, hardware, web and digital, process automation and technology roadmaps. I act as the hospital administrator, not one consultant pretending to be an expert in everything. I bring in the right specialist at the right time, brief them on your roadmap and keep the whole plan moving.

### Is YBSL a compliance consultancy?

Not in the usual sense. Compliance is the means, winning contracts is the goal. We don't sell you a certificate and walk away. We diagnose what is stopping you getting through the buyer's gates, set the right order to fix it, and coordinate specialists who understand manufacturing to do the work.

### What is the Bid & Tender Readiness Screening?

A free seven-question quiz that takes about two minutes. It scores your business against what buyers weigh most, including cyber security, insurance and finance, standards and quality, track record, social value, data protection and modern slavery, and shows you category by category where your gaps are.

### How do I get started with YBSL?

It's three simple steps. First, take the free Bid & Tender Readiness Screening, seven quick questions that show where you stand. Second, book a Comprehensive Health Assessment. We look at your business and your target tenders through the buyer's eyes, identify every gap, show which tenders you can't currently bid for and set out what it takes to qualify. Third, the Full Review. AI checks your documents against every requirement, then a bid manager with 15 years' experience evaluating tenders goes through it personally, spotting the nuances AI can't. You get a complete overhaul of your tender response and a clear roadmap, so you're ready to compete for more of the bids you go after.

### What is the Full Review?

The Full Review is a complete overhaul of your tender response. AI checks your documents against every requirement quickly and thoroughly, then a bid manager with 15 years' experience evaluating tenders across manufacturing, construction and facilities management goes through it personally. They pick up the nuances AI misses: what an evaluator is really looking for, where a good answer still loses marks, and the small details that decide close contests. You get the reworked response and a clear roadmap.

### What is Contender?

Contender is YBSL's live tender and compliance dashboard, coming soon. It watches UK tenders for you, matches them to your profile, shows a countdown to every bid deadline and alerts you the moment a compliance gap opens, such as a certificate about to lapse. You can open an example dashboard from the How It Works section of our home page.

### How is YBSL different from a bid writing agency?

A bid writer improves the words. YBSL fixes what sits behind them. Most manufacturers are filtered out at the gate, on Cyber Essentials, insurance, financial standing or a missing Carbon Reduction Plan, before the quality answers are ever read. We diagnose those gaps first, coordinate the specialists who close them, and then a bid manager makes sure the response scores.

### Can you guarantee we will win a tender?

No, and anyone who promises that is selling you something. Nobody controls a buyer's decision. What we can do is make sure you are never knocked out on a technicality, so every gate is passed and every piece of evidence is ready, and you are genuinely in a position to compete for the win on quality and price.

## Guide: Protecting the Production Line (cyber risk briefing, October 2026)

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/protecting-the-production-line.pdf

An 8-page briefing by Rob Atkins on what the 2026 cyber data means for UK manufacturers and the tenders they want to win. Headline figures it reports: manufacturing took 27.7% of all cyber attacks, the most of any sector for the fifth year running (IBM X-Force 2026); 61% of manufacturing breaches involved ransomware and 61% involved a third party such as a supplier (Verizon DBIR 2026); the Jaguar Land Rover attack cost the UK economy an estimated £2bn and hit around 5,000 supply chain firms (Cyber Monitoring Centre). It covers the five threats that matter most (ransomware, unpatched systems, supply chain attacks, phone and text scams, and intellectual property leaking through AI tools), how attackers get in, what an attack really costs, why a manufacturer is its customers' supply chain risk, and the fixes that make the biggest difference.

## Question: Do I need Cyber Essentials to bid for a government contract?
URL: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/do-i-need-cyber-essentials.html

Often, but not on every contract. Under PPN 014, central government departments, their agencies, non-departmental public bodies and NHS bodies should ask for Cyber Essentials or Cyber Essentials Plus where a contract involves personal information about citizens or government staff, ICT that stores or processes OFFICIAL data, or information about the day-to-day business of government. A contract to supply parts that touches none of that may not trigger the rule at all. Councils can choose to follow the same approach, and your bigger customers can set their own terms, so the answer for you sits in the tender documents. Here's how I'd work it out if I were in your seat.

### Who is likely to ask for it
- Central government and the NHS: PPN 014 tells these buyers to require it where the contract meets one of its data or ICT triggers. They should have the certificate in hand before award, and it has to be renewed every year for the life of the contract.
- Councils and other public bodies: PPN 014 only says they may wish to apply the same approach, so it isn't automatic. Some ask for it on everything and some don't. Check the conditions of participation on each tender rather than assuming.
- Primes, OEMs and Tier-1s: Your customer can make it a condition of doing business, whether or not any government rule applies to the job. If a prime is on a government contract, expect the question to come down the chain to you too.
- Defence work: MOD contracts and subcontracts can carry their own cyber requirements under DEFSTAN 05-138. If you're in a defence supply chain, ask which level applies to you, and don't assume a Cyber Essentials certificate settles it.

### Four traps that catch manufacturers out
- 1. The certificate has lapsed: A certificate expires after 12 months and you have to go through it again each year. Get the renewal in the diary well ahead of it, because a lapse tends to show up the week a tender closes.
- 2. The scope misses what the buyer cares about: You can certify the whole business or a well-defined, separately managed part of it, split off by a firewall or VLAN, with the boundary agreed before the assessment starts. If the buyer's data sits outside that boundary, your certificate doesn't answer their question.
- 3. Nobody has thought about the factory floor: The requirements are written for IT and don't mention production machinery. The test is whether a device can connect to or from the internet, so a connected machine could fall in scope. Settle that at the start. And remember, passing doesn't mean your machines are protected. OT and industrial cybersecurity
- 4. Your cloud services and logins were left out: Under the current requirements (version 3.3), cloud services hosting your data or services can't be excluded, and logging in to them must always use multi-factor authentication. If you last looked at this a couple of years ago, go through it again.

### Why more of your customers may start asking
When Jaguar Land Rover was hit by a cyber attack in 2025, vehicle production at its major UK plants stopped for around five weeks. The Cyber Monitoring Centre estimated the cost to the UK at £1.9 billion and said more than 5,000 organisations were affected. Some suppliers cut pay or laid off staff.
That same October, ministers wrote to the UK's biggest companies asking them to require Cyber Essentials across their supply chains. The government's voluntary Cyber Resilience Pledge now asks signatories to take a risk-based approach to this, which may include requiring it from all suppliers. So if you supply a large company, or supply someone who does, expect the question to reach you, even if you never bid for public work. Some buyers will want Cyber Essentials Plus, so check what yours expects before you choose.
JLR isn't a client of ours, and I'm not suggesting Cyber Essentials would have prevented the attack.

### Common questions
- Is Cyber Essentials a legal requirement? No. It's a government-backed certification scheme, and no law makes every business hold it. It becomes a requirement when a buyer writes it into a tender or contract, and then it can decide whether you're allowed to bid.
- How long does Cyber Essentials take? If your answers are ready, the self-assessment might take about an hour and results usually come back in about three days. If you fail, you get two working days to fix the issues and resubmit. For a manufacturer starting from scratch, I'd allow four to eight weeks, because of the work needed before you apply.
- Do I need Cyber Essentials or Cyber Essentials Plus? Follow the tender. Cyber Essentials is a verified self-assessment, and Plus adds independent technical testing. PPN 014 covers both, and the buyer decides what it needs based on risk. If the documents aren't clear, ask the buyer through the tender's clarification process.
- Can I offer something equivalent instead? PPN 014 lets suppliers show equivalent controls another way, normally verified by a technically competent, independent third party. Evidence equivalent to Plus must always be independently verified. It's usually simpler to hold the certificate than to argue the point in the middle of a bid.
- Do my subcontractors need Cyber Essentials as well? It depends on the contract. The government's Model Services Contract requires relevant subcontractors to hold it or an equivalent. Your own certificate doesn't cover third parties such as your cloud providers, so check what the buyer expects of them.

Sources: PPN 014: Cyber Essentials Scheme (GOV.UK) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-014-cyber-essentials-scheme/ppn-014-cyber-essentials-scheme-html; Cyber Essentials requirements for IT infrastructure v3.3 (NCSC) https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/files/cyber-essentials-requirements-for-it-infrastructure-v3-3.pdf; Cyber Essentials FAQs (IASME) https://iasme.co.uk/cyber-essentials/frequently-asked-questions/; Industry Security Notice 2026/02: DEFCON 658 (GOV.UK) https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69cba72ba60a12ca3913c610/ISN_2026-02_Use_of_Defence_Cyber_Certification__DCC__as_assurance_of_control_requirements_under_DEFCON_658.pdf

## Question: Should I hire a bid writer or a bid consultant?
URL: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/bid-writer-or-bid-consultant.html

Hire a bid writer if you're getting through the buyer's pass or fail checks and losing marks on your written answers. Hire a bid consultant if you're being ruled out before your answers count, or you don't know why you keep losing. A writer improves how your evidence reads. A consultant works out whether you've got the right evidence, and whether the tender is worth chasing. If you know what to say but nobody has time to run the bid, you probably need a bid manager. Get the order wrong and you can pay to polish a bid that was never going to get through. So start with where you lost. Does that make sense?

### Who does what
- Bid writer: Turns your evidence into answers that match the question and the published scoring criteria. Worth having when you've got the proof and you're losing marks on how it reads. A good writer won't invent a certificate or a track record you don't have.
- Bid manager: Runs the process: the plan, the deadlines, who supplies what, the compliance checks and the submission. Worth having when bids overlap, or when every tender turns into a last-minute scramble.
- Bid consultant: Looks at the bigger picture: are you ready, is this tender winnable, what's missing and in what order should you fix it? Worth having when you're new to tendering, keep being ruled out, or can't see a pattern in your losses.
- What if you need more than one?: Plenty of manufacturers do, because the gaps often run across certificates, insurance, finances and the written answers. That's why I coordinate specialists, including bid writers, so you're not managing them all yourself. It's also my business, so weigh my view with that in mind.

### Work it out from the last tender you lost
- 1. You failed a pass or fail question: Your answer's wording wasn't the problem. You were missing something the buyer requires, such as a turnover level, an insurance limit or a certificate. Fix that first, because a writer can't write around it. Why manufacturing bids lose
- 2. You passed, then lost marks on the answers: Read your assessment summary. Under the Procurement Act 2023, a public buyer must send one to every supplier whose tender was assessed, showing your score and the reason on each criterion. If you hold the evidence and the feedback says the answers fell short, a writer is the right call.
- 3. You lost marks because you had no proof: If the feedback points at missing case studies, data or policies, better writing only goes so far. Build the evidence first with someone who knows what buyers look for, then bring in a writer for the next one.
- 4. You ran out of time: If documents were scattered and the bid went in thin, your problem is how the bid was run. A bid manager and a proper evidence library will do more for you than another writer. Process automation

### What one pass or fail question can do
On a Royal Navy support contract worth around £385 million, MLS (Overseas) scored highest on quality and offered the lowest price. It was still disqualified for failing a pass or fail question on supply chain safety. The High Court later ruled the disqualification unlawful, because the tender hadn't made clear that failing that question meant being ruled out. So MLS had to go to court to overturn it. No amount of good writing would have fixed that question. MLS isn't a client of ours.

### Common questions
- Should a first-time bidder hire a bid writer? Only once you've checked you can meet the requirements. On a first tender, the biggest risk is often a condition you didn't know about, so go through the conditions of participation before you pay anyone to write. Then decide what help you need with the answers.
- What should I ask a bid writer before hiring them? Have they written tenders for manufacturers? Who exactly will write yours? Is the fee fixed and agreed in writing before they start? Do they use AI, and who checks what it produces? And what will they need from your team, and by when? A good writer will welcome all of those.
- How is bid support usually charged? Usually as a fixed fee per bid, a day rate or a retainer. The cost tends to follow the number of scored questions, how much evidence already exists and how tight the deadline is. Ask for a quote based on the actual tender documents, so you can compare like with like.
- Should I employ a bid writer rather than outsource? It comes down to how often you bid. If tenders come in a steady stream, having someone in-house can make sense. If you bid a handful of times a year, a full-time role is hard to keep busy, so outside support is usually the better fit.
- Can a bid writer or consultant guarantee we'll win? No, and I'd be wary of anyone who says they can. Nobody controls a buyer's decision. What good support can do is stop you being knocked out on a technicality and make sure your answers do your business justice.

Sources: Procurement Act 2023: assessment summaries (GOV.WALES) https://www.gov.wales/procurement-act-2023-guidance-assessment-summaries-html

## Question: Do I need a Carbon Reduction Plan to bid?
URL: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/do-i-need-a-carbon-reduction-plan.html

On central government contracts worth more than £5 million a year including VAT, usually yes. From 1 April 2027, NHS rules reach further, down to procurements below £5 million a year that are above the published procurement thresholds. Elsewhere it's down to the buyer. Here's the part worth knowing: under the central government guidance, the plan is pass or fail and your emissions figures aren't what's being assessed. A foundry with a big footprint can pass. A clean assembly shop with an out-of-date plan can fail. So what you need is a plan that's complete, current and signed off, and that takes data most manufacturers haven't pulled together.

### Who is likely to ask for one
- Central government: PPN 006 applies to departments, their agencies and non-departmental public bodies on contracts above £5 million a year including VAT, unless it isn't relevant or proportionate. The value is averaged over the contract's life, so a four-year contract worth £21 million is in scope.
- The NHS, from 1 April 2027: At £5 million a year or more, and on new frameworks and dynamic markets by default, the 2027 NHS plan applies and covers all relevant Scope 3 emissions. Below £5 million but above the procurement thresholds, a plan with the shorter Scope 3 list applies. Procurements started earlier stay under the old rules.
- Wales, councils and other buyers: Wales has its own policy note, WPPN 006. Councils and other public bodies can set their own requirements, so read the conditions of participation on each tender.
- Primes and larger customers: If a bigger customer needs to report on its supply chain, or is bidding for public work itself, it may ask you for a plan as a condition of doing business, even when your own contract is well under £5 million.

### What gets a plan failed
- 1. Nothing on net zero: The plan has to commit to net zero by 2050 at the latest for your UK operations. Leave that out and it fails, however good the rest of it is. Carbon Reduction Plans and ESG
- 2. Missing Scope 3 categories: You need all of Scope 1 and 2, plus five Scope 3 categories: upstream transport, waste from your operations, business travel, employee commuting and downstream transport. For a manufacturer, that means inbound freight and deliveries to customers. Leaving out a required Scope without explaining why is a fail.
- 3. Out-of-date figures: A reporting period more than 18 months old fails unless you can explain why. The plan should be reviewed and updated every year, within six months of your financial year-end, so one you wrote two years ago for a tender may no longer count.
- 4. No sign-off, or nowhere to find it: The board has to approve it and a director has to sign it. It also has to set out your environmental management measures, and be published on your UK website with a link in a prominent place on your homepage.

### Common questions
- Is a Carbon Reduction Plan a legal requirement? No general law says every manufacturer must have one. It's a condition buyers set for taking part in a tender. Larger companies may have separate carbon reporting duties under Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting, so check that with your accountant.
- Are our emissions figures scored? Not under the central government guidance. The compliance questions are pass or fail, and your baseline and current emissions are for information only. Other buyers can treat it differently, and carbon commitments can also come up in social value or contract terms, so read each tender's criteria.
- Can we use our parent company's plan? Under PPN 006, only in limited circumstances: the bidder must be wholly owned by the parent, adopt its commitment and publish the plan on its own website. PPN 006 treats this as a temporary measure until the bidder has a plan of its own.
- What if we've been trading for less than a year? The guidance says suppliers trading for under 12 months shouldn't be disadvantaged. You should confirm your commitment to net zero by 2050 and publish a full plan as soon as you can.
- Do we need one if we're bidding as a consortium? Yes. The central government guidance says each consortium member should complete its own plan, so check your partners have theirs in good time.
- Will a central government plan meet the NHS rules? Not necessarily. From 1 April 2027, the NHS plan for procurements of £5 million a year or more needs all relevant Scope 3 emissions, not just the five categories, and has its own rules on net zero. Check the NHS England guidance that applies to your tender.

Sources: PPN 006: Carbon Reduction Plans (GOV.UK) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-006-taking-account-of-carbon-reduction-plans-in-the-procurement-of-major-government-contracts/ppn-006-taking-account-of-carbon-reduction-plans-html; PPN 006 guidance on conditions of participation (GOV.UK) https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/67b716f078dd6cacb71c6a87/2025-02-05_PPN_006_Guidance_on_taking_account_of_carbon_reduction_plans_-_adopting_and_applying_conditions_of_participation.docx.pdf; PPN 006 technical standard (GOV.UK) https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/67b334c67c070e71525f5818/PPN_006_Technical_standard_for_Completion_of_Carbon_Reduction_Plans.pdf; 2027 NHS Carbon Reduction Plan requirements (NHS England) https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/2027-nhs-carbon-reduction-plan-requirements-for-the-procurement-of-nhs-goods-services-and-works/; WPPN 006: Carbon Reduction Plans in Wales (GOV.WALES) https://www.gov.wales/wppn-006-decarbonisation-through-procurement-taking-account-of-carbon-reduction-plans-html

## Guide: What the government's FTSE 350 cyber letter means for UK manufacturers
URL: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/ftse-350-cyber-letter-for-manufacturers.html
PDF: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/ftse-350-cyber-letter-for-manufacturers.pdf

On 13 October 2025, senior ministers and the heads of the National Cyber Security Centre and the National Crime Agency wrote to the chief executives and chairs of every FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 company, and a number of other leading UK firms, with three requests. The third was to require Cyber Essentials in their supply chains. If you supply one of those companies, or supply someone who does, that request could reach you as a condition of doing business, even if you never bid for public work. It's a request and not a law, and every customer will move at its own speed. But it's better to be ready before they ask than to find out when they do. Here's what the letter says and what I'd do about it.

### What the letter asks boards to do
- 1. Make cyber risk a Board-level priority: Use the government's Cyber Governance Code of Practice, and complete the free training that goes with it. The letter also asks boards to plan and rehearse how they'd keep operating and rebuild after a destructive attack.
- 2. Sign up to NCSC Early Warning: This free service tells you about potential cyber attacks on your network. The letter strongly advises companies and their suppliers to register, so this one is meant for you too.
- 3. Require Cyber Essentials in the supply chain: The letter calls Cyber Essentials the minimum standard businesses should seek. It says government already requires most of its suppliers to meet it, and asks the country's largest businesses to embed the same requirements in their own supply chains.
- Who signed it: Liz Kendall, Rachel Reeves, Peter Kyle and Dan Jarvis signed for the government, alongside Dr Richard Horne, CEO of the National Cyber Security Centre, and Graeme Biggar, Director General of the National Crime Agency. Read the letter on GOV.UK

### What it means for your business
- Your customers may start asking: The letter says just 14% of UK businesses assess the cyber risks posed by their immediate suppliers. The government's voluntary Cyber Resilience Pledge now asks signatories to take a risk-based approach to requiring Cyber Essentials, which may include requiring it from all suppliers.
- It can reach you outside a tender: You don't have to bid for public work to feel this. A large customer can make Cyber Essentials part of its supplier checks or contract terms, and that can pass down from one tier to the next. Do I need Cyber Essentials?
- There's a balance sheet argument too: The letter says organisations with Cyber Essentials are 92% less likely to make a claim on their cyber insurance. For a manufacturer, that's a good reason to look at it, even before a customer asks.
- What the letter doesn't say: It doesn't make Cyber Essentials a legal requirement, it doesn't set a deadline for suppliers, and it doesn't mention Cyber Essentials Plus. Some buyers ask for Plus anyway, so check what yours expects.

### Common questions
- Does the letter make Cyber Essentials a legal requirement? No. It's a request from government to the boards of leading companies. It becomes binding on you if a customer writes it into its supplier terms or contract, or if a tender makes it a condition.
- My business isn't in the FTSE 350. Does this affect me? It can, if you supply a company that acts on the letter or supply someone who does. Whether it reaches you, and when, depends on what your customers decide to do.
- What is Cyber Essentials? A government-backed scheme that certifies you have key protections in place against common cyber attacks. It covers firewalls, secure configuration, security update management, user access control and malware protection.
- What is the Cyber Resilience Pledge? A voluntary government pledge for major organisations. Signatories commit to board responsibility for cyber risk, signing up to Early Warning and a risk-based approach to requiring Cyber Essentials across their supply chains.

## Guide: Protecting the Production Line: what the 2026 cyber data means for UK manufacturers
URL: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/protecting-the-production-line.html
PDF: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/protecting-the-production-line.pdf

If you run a UK manufacturing business, your production line is now the most attacked target in the economy, and your cyber position is quietly deciding which tenders you can even bid for. I've spent 30 years selling technology into businesses like yours, and the pattern never changes. The MD knows cyber matters, it sits on the list, then a big order lands and it slips another quarter. This briefing pulls together the latest 2026 figures and keeps only what a busy MD needs: what's hitting manufacturers, what it costs and the handful of things that make the biggest difference. Is that okay? Good, let's get into it.

### Manufacturing by the numbers, 2026
- 27.7% of all attacks: Manufacturing took more cyber attacks than any other sector last year, for the fifth year running (IBM X-Force 2026).
- 61% ransomware: Of manufacturing breaches involved ransomware, and malware of some kind was in 75% (Verizon DBIR 2026).
- 61% third party: Of manufacturing breaches involved a supplier, vendor or partner (Verizon DBIR 2026).
- £3m per UK breach: The average cost of a UK breach, with about 225 days to find and contain it (IBM UK Cost of a Data Breach 2026). The worldwide average for industrial businesses is £4m.
- 87% about money: Of attacks are financially motivated, and a further 15% are espionage, after your designs (Verizon DBIR 2026).
- 43% of UK businesses: Were hit by a breach or attack in the last year, rising to 69% of large firms (UK Cyber Breaches Survey 2025/26).
- 1,589 attempts a week: The number of attack attempts per UK organisation every week, up 34% on a year ago (Check Point, June 2026).
- Only 31% at board level: Of UK businesses have someone at board level responsible for cyber, and only 25% have a written incident response plan.

### The five threats that matter most
- Ransomware: Involved in 61% of manufacturing breaches. Your systems are locked and your data stolen until you pay, or rebuild.
- Unpatched systems: 38% of breaches started with an exploited weakness in kit facing the internet. It's now the number one way in.
- Supply chain attacks: 61% of breaches involved a third party. Someone else's weak spot becomes your problem, and yours becomes your customer's.
- Phone and text scams: 40% more likely to work than an email. The fake call from IT asking for a code is the scam to watch.
- Intellectual property leaking through AI: 45% of staff now use AI regularly at work, 67% of them through personal accounts. Drawings, specs and source code are being pasted into tools you don't control.

### What it really costs
- Jaguar Land Rover, UK, 2025: Five weeks with no car production, an estimated £1.9 billion cost to the UK economy and more than 5,000 organisations affected (Cyber Monitoring Centre).
- Asahi Group, Japan, late 2025: Ransomware closed its domestic factories, suspended shipments and put corporate data at risk.
- Kreisel GmbH, Germany, 2024: Ransomware halted operations for weeks. It refused to pay, never recovered and filed for insolvency that November.
- Why that matters to you: JLR had the size and the balance sheet to ride it out. Kreisel didn't. Most of the manufacturers I talk to in Essex, Kent and London look a lot more like Kreisel than JLR. Does that make sense?

### The fundamentals checklist
- 1. Patch fast: Patch anything facing the internet within 14 days of a critical fix, and know who owns that job.
- 2. Multi-factor authentication: Turn it on for email, remote access and every cloud system.
- 3. Clean up accounts: Remove old accounts and limit admin rights to the few people who need them.
- 4. Backups you can trust: Keep offline or immutable backups, and test a restore at least twice a year.
- 5. Separate production: Separate your production network (OT) from the office network. OT and industrial cybersecurity
- 6. Brief your staff: Warn them about phone and text scams, with a simple call back to check rule.
- 7. One-page AI policy: Write it down and name the tools people are allowed to use.
- 8. Check suppliers: Ask key suppliers about their cyber standards and put a minimum in the contract.
- 9. Plan the first hour: Write down who does what in the first hour of an attack, including who rings the insurer.
- 10. Get certified: Get Cyber Essentials, then decide whether buyers need Plus or ISO 27001. Do I need Cyber Essentials?

### Common questions
- How do attackers get into manufacturers? The most common way in is now an unpatched system facing the internet, at 38% of manufacturing breaches, ahead of phishing at 13% and stolen logins at 11% (Verizon DBIR 2026). Stolen credentials featured in 41% of manufacturing breaches overall.
- What is the first thing a manufacturer should fix? Patch anything facing the internet and turn on multi-factor authentication for email, remote access and every cloud system. None of this needs a genius hacker. It needs a gap that nobody has got round to closing, and gaps can be closed.
- Should we ban AI tools to protect our designs? No. Pick approved tools, write a one-page policy and tell people what they can and can't paste in. Verizon found 3.2% of uploads were research and technical documentation, so expect buyers to start asking about it.
- Does Cyber Essentials reduce insurance claims? The UK Government says organisations with Cyber Essentials are 92% less likely to make a claim on their cyber insurance.

## Guide: The Compliance Reality for UK Manufacturers: what fines you, what costs you the contract and what's coming
URL: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/compliance-reality-for-uk-manufacturers.html
PDF: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/compliance-reality-for-uk-manufacturers.pdf

It can be tempting to put compliance on the back burner, but addressing it now can save you significant time, cost and stress later. Public sector buyers, and increasingly the large private customers above you in the supply chain, no longer just ask whether you can make the product. They ask whether you are safe, legal, insured, certified and demonstrably responsible before they'll let you near a contract. Two distinctions run through this guide. Some things fine you: health and safety, employment law and data protection are enforced by regulators. Others cost you the contract: requirements like Cyber Essentials, insurance, financial standing and social value carry no government fine, but where a buyer asks for them they can rule you out or out-score you.

### What fines you today
- Employment law changed on 6 April 2026: The Employment Rights Act 2025 is law. Statutory sick pay and paternity and parental leave are now day-one rights, the protective award for getting a collective redundancy wrong has doubled to 180 days' pay per employee, and a new Fair Work Agency began enforcing on 7 April 2026. From 1 January 2027 the unfair dismissal qualifying period drops from two years to six months. People and employment law
- Health and safety carries the heaviest fines: HSE fines scale with turnover and run into millions for serious breaches. The Corporate Manslaughter Act carries unlimited fines and directors can face personal prosecution. It's also assessed at the Selection Questionnaire stage on virtually every public contract. Health and safety
- A data breach can cost up to £17.5m or 4% of turnover: UK GDPR is fully in force, and a reportable breach must reach the ICO within 72 hours. If you process a customer's data, your Data Processing Agreement pins the liability on you. GDPR and data protection

### What costs you the contract
- Cyber Essentials: On many contracts it's the floor you must clear even to bid. Where a tender requires it, you're out without it, and if a required certificate lapses you can breach the contract. Do I need Cyber Essentials?
- Insurance: Public and Employers' Liability, Professional Indemnity and Product Liability must be held at the levels the buyer specifies, with certificates in the right format. Under-insured, wrong format or missing a policy can be a straightforward fail. Insurance and key person cover
- Financial standing: Buyers check turnover against contract value, filed accounts and ratios such as current ratio, gearing and interest cover. Newer businesses without three years of filed history need the right management accounts and accountant's letters. Financial standing
- ISO certifications: ISO 9001 is table stakes. ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 are increasingly required, and ISO 27001 appears on larger or data-heavy contracts. Many manufacturers hold 9001 alone and are quietly screened out of everything that asks for the others. ISO management systems
- Social value: Under the Procurement Act 2023, award moved to the most advantageous tender. Manufacturers already do local hiring, apprenticeships and community work but can't evidence or quantify it, so they leave those marks on the table. Bid writing
- Carbon: Statutory carbon reporting (SECR) applies only to large companies. Below that there's no general legal duty, but buyers can ask for a Carbon Reduction Plan and Scope 1, 2 and 3 data whatever your size. Do I need a Carbon Reduction Plan?
- Modern Slavery: A statement is a legal obligation only once turnover reaches £36m. Larger customers require one in their tender questions anyway, and evaluators check your website for it. People and employment law
- Contract terms: Standard terms often set liability caps and clauses that conflict with your insurance or operating model. Missing an Anti-Bribery or Whistleblowing policy is also a common questionnaire fail. Contract review
- Your website: During due diligence, evaluators can go straight to your site to verify your certifications, Carbon Reduction Plan, Modern Slavery statement and privacy policy. Stale logos or missing policies can sink a good bid. Web design and digital

### What is coming over the next five years
- Cyber Security and Resilience Bill: Not law when this guide was written, with phased implementation possibly running to 2028. Manufacturing isn't currently named in direct scope, but it regulates managed service providers and creates designated critical suppliers, and large customers may push requirements down to you by contract.
- Ransomware rules: The proposed payment ban targets the public sector and critical national infrastructure. A duty to notify before paying and mandatory incident reporting may reach everyone else, so tested offline backups and a rehearsed continuity plan matter. Managed IT
- EU Cyber Resilience Act: Since 11 September 2026, manufacturers of products with digital elements have had to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents. If you sell anything with software or connectivity into Europe, the clock is already running. OT and industrial cybersecurity
- Joining it all up: Sixteen separate suppliers can produce sixteen documents that contradict each other under scrutiny. A lapsed certificate, an out-of-date website and a missing policy compound. Technology roadmap

### Common questions
- What can a UK manufacturer be fined for? Health and safety, employment law and data protection are enforced by regulators. HSE fines scale with turnover, and the ICO can fine up to £17.5m or 4% of global annual turnover under UK GDPR.
- Is a Modern Slavery statement a legal requirement? Only once turnover reaches £36m. Most manufacturers with 10 to 500 employees sit under that, but larger customers can still ask for one in their tender questions.
- What changed in employment law in 2026? The Employment Rights Act 2025 brought day-one rights to statutory sick pay and paternity and parental leave from 6 April 2026, doubled the protective award to 180 days' pay and created a Fair Work Agency. From 1 January 2027, the unfair dismissal qualifying period drops to six months.

## Bid Writing and Tenders

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/bid-writing-tenders.html

**Turning your evidence into an answer that actually scores.**

Compliance only wins contracts if it is communicated the way evaluators score. Manufacturers who clear every hurdle still lose regularly on weak quality or methodology answers.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without dedicated bid writing, the bid itself under-delivers strong capability reads as a weak, generic answer, evidence exists but never reaches the section that would score it, responses answer what you want to say, not what was asked, inconsistent quality across sections written by different people and submissions rushed and non-compliant with format requirements.
You can be the best manufacturer on the list and still come fourth, because someone else answered the question that was actually asked.

### The point most people miss

Most manufacturers think tenders are won by writing. High-performing manufacturers know they are won by evidence. If the fifteen sections before this one are in order, the bid almost writes itself, because every answer already has a document behind it.
Tender writing is not writing documents. It is strategic storytelling backed by evidence, and this is where the whole model pays off.

### What it covers

#### Strategy & Readiness

Tender readiness assessments and bid strategy built around the scoring criteria.

#### Response Writing

Quality, methodology and social value answers written to how evaluators actually mark.

#### Evidence Mapping

Case studies, risk, ESG, cyber and workforce evidence embedded into the right section.

#### Submission Management

Compliance checks, portal submission and post-result debriefs.

### What it looks like inside a manufacturer

- Tender readiness reviewed quarterly, not the week a bid lands.
- An evidence library maintained and updated.
- Case studies refreshed annually.
- Policies and certificates stored centrally where the bid writer can reach them.
- Responses written to the scoring criteria, in the order they are scored.
- Risk, ESG, cyber and workforce evidence embedded rather than appended.
- Compliance checks run before submission.
- Feedback analysed after every result, win or lose.

### Bid/Tender scoring impact

| Tender criterion | What this service contributes | Score effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quality | Directly written and scored | Major |
| Risk | Risk evidence structured and mapped to criteria | Major |
| ESG | Social value answers directly written and scored | Major |
| Compliance | A fully compliant submission | Major |
| Experience | Case studies presented as scored evidence | Major |
| Delivery | Clear operational capability | Moderate |
| Innovation | Differentiation and win themes | Moderate |

### What it strengthens

- Every other Cure Alliance service — this is where their evidence gets scored.
- ISO Consultant — process maturity becomes a written quality answer.
- Sustainability / ESG — environmental commitments become social value marks.
- Training and Skills — competence evidence becomes method statement content.

### Common questions about bid writing and tenders

**Why do good manufacturers lose tenders they should win?**
Usually because the answer did not match the question, not because the capability was missing. Evaluators mark quality and method statements against published criteria, in the order they are written. A generic answer that talks about what you do well, rather than what was asked, loses marks even when the evidence exists somewhere in the business. Answer in scoring order, and put a document behind every claim.

**How much is social value worth in a government tender?**
At least 10% of the total score on central government contracts. Under PPN 002, central government departments, agencies and non-departmental public bodies must give social value a minimum 10% weighting on procurements under the Procurement Act 2023 started on or after 1 October 2025. On a close contest, that 10% is often the whole margin between first and second.

**What should a manufacturer have ready before a tender lands?**
An evidence library you can draw on in minutes. That means current certificates, your insurance schedule, the last two or three years of accounts, your key policies, three recent case studies, a training matrix and, for larger government work, a published Carbon Reduction Plan. Review it every quarter, not the week a bid arrives.

Sources: PPN 002: Social value in central government contracts (GOV.UK) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html

## Contract Review

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/commercial-solicitor.html

**Proving you know what you're agreeing to before you sign.**

Buyer contracts are drafted to protect the buyer. Every clause you accept without reading it has a price, whether or not you ever put a number on it.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without contract review, you risk signing liability terms your insurance doesn't actually cover, missing TUPE obligations that create workforce and legal exposure, one-sided termination clauses with no negotiated protection, undocumented conflicts of interest surfacing later and disputes with no clear contractual escalation path.
None of that shows up at tender stage — it shows up during delivery, when it's expensive to fix.

### The point most people miss

Most manufacturers think contract review is a legal formality. It is a commercial one. Uncapped liability, ninety-day payment terms and free tooling all have a price, whether you calculate it or not.
The point is not to make you difficult to deal with. It is to make sure that when you quote a job, you know what you are actually agreeing to carry.

### What it covers

#### Contract Review

Redlining standard terms, force majeure, liability caps and termination clauses.

#### Governance Policies

Anti-Bribery & Corruption and Whistleblowing policies drafted and followed.

#### Workforce & Transfer

TUPE advisory for contracts involving staff transfer.

#### Risk & Disputes

Conflict of interest declarations and a known escalation process for disputes.

### What it looks like inside a manufacturer

- Contracts are reviewed before signature, not after a problem arises.
- Liability caps are understood and matched against actual insurance cover.
- Termination and force majeure clauses are known, not discovered under pressure.
- TUPE risk is assessed before a contract that involves staff transfer is signed.
- Sub-contractor agreements mirror the obligations in the head contract.
- Disputes are escalated through a known process, not improvised.
- Someone qualified has actually read the contract you're about to sign.

### Bid/Tender scoring impact

| Tender criterion | What this service contributes | Score effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Risk | Onerous terms identified and negotiated before signature | Major |
| Compliance | Anti-Bribery and Whistleblowing policies often required | Moderate |
| Financial Standing | Liability caps protect financial exposure | Moderate |
| Delivery | Clear terms reduce dispute-driven delivery risk | Moderate |
| Quality | Governance policies support process maturity narrative | Minor |

### What it strengthens

- Insurance Broking & Key Person Cover — liability caps must match cover in place.
- Chartered Accountant — financial exposure is set by contract terms.
- HR & Employment Law — TUPE and workforce terms overlap directly.
- Bid Writing & Tenders — governance policies feed compliance appendices.

### Common questions about contract review

**What should I check in a buyer's contract before I sign?**
Six things, every time: the liability cap and whether your insurance actually covers it, payment terms, termination and force majeure, who owns the tooling and intellectual property, any TUPE obligations, and whether your subcontractor agreements carry the same obligations down the chain. Each one has a price, whether you calculate it or not.

**Do I need anti-bribery and whistleblowing policies to bid?**
Very often, yes. Selection questionnaires regularly ask for them, and the Procurement Act 2023 lets buyers exclude suppliers connected with offences such as bribery and fraud. A written policy that people actually follow is the simplest way to show a buyer your governance is real.

**What is TUPE, and when does it apply to a contract?**
TUPE protects employees' terms when a business or service moves from one employer to another. It can apply when a service contract changes hands and staff move with it, which is common in outsourced and facilities work. If a contract might involve staff transferring to you, assess the cost before you price the bid, not after you have won it.

Sources: Procurement Act 2023 (legislation.gov.uk) https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/54/contents; TUPE: employee rights when a business changes hands (GOV.UK) https://www.gov.uk/transfers-takeovers

## Financial Standing

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/financial-standing.html

**Proving you'll still be trading when the contract ends.**

Financial standing is the first thing a buyer checks, and it is often automated. A threshold gets set — typically twice the annual contract value — and bids below it never reach a human reader.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without current, well-presented financials, a buyer assumes insufficient turnover to safely deliver the contract, cash flow that can't absorb mobilisation costs, outdated or unreliable financial reporting, undisclosed tax or compliance risk and a business growing faster than its financial controls.
None of that may be true of you. It does not matter. In a tender, the assumption is what gets scored.

### The point most people miss

Most manufacturers think their accountant's job ends at the tax return. It does not. The moment you bid for a contract worth more than half your turnover, your books stop being paperwork and start being evidence.
Nobody negotiates with a financial threshold. You either clear it or you are filtered out before anyone reads a word you wrote.

### What it covers

#### Financial Standing

Turnover thresholds, filed accounts and management accounts that clear the buyer's minimum bar.

#### Tax & Compliance

Corporation tax, PAYE, VAT and NIC confirmed and evidenced, not just assumed.

#### Cash Flow & Ratios

Forecasting and ratio monitoring that proves you can absorb mobilisation costs.

#### Credit & Reporting

Credit rating management and cloud accounting built for contract-specific reporting.

### What it looks like inside a manufacturer

- Filed accounts are current and match what's declared in the bid.
- Management accounts exist and are current if statutory accounts lag.
- Turnover comfortably clears the threshold buyers set against contract value.
- Tax compliance is confirmed and evidenced, not just assumed.
- Financial ratios are monitored, not discovered for the first time in a tender.
- Cash flow is modelled against contract mobilisation costs.
- Credit score is checked and understood before it surprises anyone.
- Financial documentation is ready to submit without a scramble.

### Bid/Tender scoring impact

| Tender criterion | What this service contributes | Score effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Financial Standing | Direct evidence against the buyer's minimum threshold | Major |
| Risk | Ratios and solvency read directly as continuity risk | Major |
| Compliance | Tax and filing compliance confirmed | Major |
| Delivery | Cash flow capacity to mobilise and deliver | Moderate |
| Quality | Clean financial systems support wider process evidence | Moderate |

### What it strengthens

- Insurance Broking & Key Person Cover — financial and insurance standing are read together.
- Commercial Solicitor — liability caps are set against what the business can bear.
- Bid Writing & Tenders — financial evidence underpins every capability claim.
- vCIO Technology Advisory — investment decisions are grounded in real numbers.

### Common questions about financial standing

**How much turnover do I need to bid for a contract?**
Buyers commonly set a minimum turnover of around twice the annual contract value, and many check it automatically. If a contract is worth more than half your turnover, expect your accounts to be scrutinised closely. Check the selection questionnaire for the exact figure on every tender, because it varies.

**What financial evidence do buyers ask for?**
Usually your last two or three years of filed accounts, plus management accounts if your statutory accounts are out of date. Many buyers also run a credit check through a credit reference agency, and some ask for a bank reference. Make sure what you declare in the bid matches exactly what Companies House shows.

**Can a young or fast-growing manufacturer pass financial standing?**
Often, yes, if you prepare for it. Current management accounts, a parent company guarantee or a performance bond can all help, and a short, honest explanation of a one-off dip reads far better than silence. The mistake is letting an automated check make the decision before anyone sees the context.

## Insurance and Key Person Cover

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/insurance-key-person.html

**Proving the financial hit lands on your insurer, not theirs.**

When something goes wrong on a contract, the buyer wants to know the financial hit lands on your insurer, not on them. Cover levels and formats get checked early, and mechanically.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without correctly structured insurance, a buyer assumes underinsured exposure, a business one bad event away from collapse, no continuity plan if a key person leaves or falls ill, mismatched liability between contract and cover and administrative carelessness that suggests wider carelessness.
None of that may be true of you. It does not matter. In a tender, the assumption is what gets scored.

### The point most people miss

Most manufacturers assume their broker sorted this years ago and never revisit it. Cover quietly falls out of date while the business, and the contracts it bids for, grow past it.
Insurance is not a policy document in a drawer. It is proof that the business is professionally run.

### What it covers

#### Core Business Cover

Public liability, employers' liability, professional indemnity and product liability at buyer-specified minimums.

#### Cyber & Continuity

Cyber liability aligned to your certification, plus business interruption and machinery breakdown cover.

#### Key Person Protection

Cover for the founder or critical-skill dependency that would stop delivery if they were gone.

#### Evidence & Renewal

Cover checked against every tender, certificates in the right format, renewals tracked against the pipeline.

### What it looks like inside a manufacturer

- Cover levels are checked against each tender before submission, not assumed.
- Certificates are in the exact format the procurement portal requires.
- Key person cover exists for anyone whose absence would stop delivery.
- Cyber and PI cover are aligned with actual contractual liability.
- Machinery breakdown cover is in place for the equipment that would stop you.
- Renewal dates are tracked against the bid pipeline, not just the calendar.
- Insurance schedules are reviewed annually against business growth.
- Claims history is documented and explainable.

### Bid/Tender scoring impact

| Tender criterion | What this service contributes | Score effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Risk | Cover levels read directly as financial resilience | Major |
| Compliance | Cover matched to Selection Questionnaire minimums | Major |
| Financial Standing | Signals a business built to survive disruption | Major |
| Delivery | Machinery breakdown and business interruption cover protect delivery | Moderate |
| Safety | Correctly formatted certificates avoid disqualification | Moderate |

### What it strengthens

- Chartered Accountant — insurance and financial standing are read together.
- Cyber Security / vCISO — cyber liability cover depends on certified controls.
- Commercial Solicitor — liability caps in contracts must match cover in place.
- Health & Safety — incident history feeds both H&S and insurance risk profile.

### Common questions about insurance and key person cover

**What insurance do I need to bid for public sector contracts?**
Employers' liability is a legal requirement, with a minimum of £5 million of cover. On top of that, tenders commonly specify public liability, often at £5 million to £10 million, plus professional indemnity and product liability depending on what you supply. The figure that matters is the one in each selection questionnaire, so check it every time.

**Why do bids get rejected over insurance?**
Usually for mechanical reasons, not because the business is uninsured. The cover is below the stated minimum, the certificate has expired, the policyholder name does not match the company that is bidding, or the limit is on an aggregate basis when the buyer asked for each and every claim. All four are easy to fix before submission and impossible to fix after.

**What is key person insurance, and do buyers care about it?**
Key person insurance pays out if someone the business depends on, often the founder or a lead engineer, dies or becomes critically ill. Buyers care because they score continuity risk. If one person's absence would stop delivery, a buyer will notice, and cover plus a succession plan is the answer they want to see.

Sources: Employers' liability insurance (GOV.UK) https://www.gov.uk/employers-liability-insurance

## Health and Safety

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/health-safety.html

**Proving your site won't hurt anyone, on paper and on the floor.**

Health and safety is checked on almost every public-sector tender, and it is checked hard. A missing or lapsed accreditation is one of the fastest ways an otherwise strong bid gets screened out.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without current H&S accreditation, a buyer assumes an uncontrolled or poorly supervised site, higher likelihood of incidents and delivery disruption, weak duty-of-care toward your own people, accreditation that has lapsed without anyone noticing and a business that reacts to incidents rather than preventing them.
None of that may be true of you. It does not matter. In a tender, the assumption is what gets scored.

### The point most people miss

Most manufacturers think of H&S as paperwork that sits in a folder. Auditors do not read the folder first. They walk the floor, then check whether the paperwork matches what they just saw.
Buyers do not want a policy document. They want proof that if something goes wrong on your shop floor, you already know what happens next.

### What it covers

#### Policy & Risk Assessment

Written H&S policy, risk assessments and method statements specific to your actual operations.

#### Accreditation

SafeContractor, Achilles or an equivalent SSIP scheme, current and matched to the accrediting body's register.

#### Incident Management

RIDDOR reporting, accident tracking and corrective actions tracked to closure.

#### Site Discipline

PPE, inductions, machinery inspection records and a named person with real authority to act.

### What it looks like inside a manufacturer

- Risk assessments are specific to the actual operations, not generic templates.
- Accreditation certificates are current and match the accrediting body's register.
- Accident and near-miss logs are maintained and reviewed, not filed and forgotten.
- Machinery has current maintenance and safety inspection records.
- Staff can describe the evacuation plan without prompting.
- Inductions happen before anyone new sets foot on the shop floor.
- Corrective actions from incidents are tracked to closure.
- A named person owns H&S with real authority to act.

### Bid/Tender scoring impact

| Tender criterion | What this service contributes | Score effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Safety | Direct, primary evidence category | Major |
| Risk | Incident history and controls read as operational risk | Major |
| Compliance | Accreditation is a stated SQ gateway requirement | Major |
| Quality | Documented procedures signal process maturity | Moderate |
| Delivery | Fewer incidents means fewer delivery disruptions | Moderate |

### What it strengthens

- ISO Consultant — the certified extension of the same discipline.
- Training and Skills — competence records underpin safe operation.
- Insurance Broking & Key Person Cover — claims history and premiums track H&S performance.
- OT / ICS Security — physical and operational safety share the same audit trail.

### Common questions about health and safety

**Which health and safety accreditation do I need for tenders?**
Most buyers accept a scheme that belongs to Safety Schemes in Procurement (SSIP), such as CHAS, SafeContractor or Achilles. Some ask for ISO 45001 instead, particularly on larger or higher-risk contracts. Check which one the buyer names before you spend money, because the right single certificate often covers several buyers.

**What does SSIP deem to satisfy mean?**
It means SSIP member schemes recognise each other's core health and safety assessment. If you hold one SSIP certificate and a buyer asks for a different SSIP scheme, you can usually get recognised without paying for a full second assessment. It saves time and money, but only if your certificate is current and shows on the scheme's register.

**What health and safety evidence do evaluators actually check?**
Proof that your paperwork matches your shop floor. That means risk assessments specific to your operations, an accident and near-miss log, RIDDOR reports where required, machinery inspection records, training records and a current certificate that matches the accrediting body's register. Generic templates are spotted quickly.

Sources: Safety Schemes in Procurement (SSIP) https://ssip.org.uk/; RIDDOR reporting (HSE) https://www.hse.gov.uk/riddor/

## ISO Management Systems

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/iso-standards.html

**Proving you are controlled, consistent and audit-ready.**

ISO is the discipline that proves you are controlled, consistent, safe and audit-ready. In the Cure Alliance model it is the backbone, because almost every other service leans on the evidence it produces.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without ISO, a buyer assumes inconsistent processes, uncontrolled risks, weak governance, unreliable delivery, poor evidence and high operational volatility.
None of that may be true of you. It does not matter. In a tender, the assumption is what gets scored.

### The point most people miss

Buyers, especially OEMs and Tier-1s, use ISO as a risk filter. If you have it, you are low risk. If you do not, you are high risk, regardless of how good you actually are.
People think ISO is paperwork. It is not. ISO is predictability, and predictability is what buyers want and pay for.

### What it covers

#### Quality — ISO 9001

Process control, consistency and the paper trail that proves it.

#### Environmental — ISO 14001

Environmental responsibility built into how the business runs.

#### Health & Safety — ISO 45001

The certified extension of your day-to-day safety discipline.

#### Governance & Audit

Management reviews, internal audits, document control and risk-based thinking.

### What it looks like inside a manufacturer

- Processes are controlled, and responsibilities are defined.
- Procedures are documented, and people actually follow them.
- Training and competence records are current.
- Calibration and maintenance logs are up to date.
- Suppliers are assured, not assumed.
- Non-conformances are managed rather than argued about.
- Audit trails exist and stand up to scrutiny.
- Environmental controls and safety risk assessments are in place.
- Incidents get reported and reviewed.
- Management oversight is documented, not implied.

### Bid/Tender scoring impact

| Tender criterion | What this service contributes | Score effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quality | Process control and hard evidence | Major |
| Experience | Case studies backed by ISO maturity | Moderate |
| ESG | ISO 14001 plus DEI evidence | Major |
| Safety | ISO 45001 | Major |
| Innovation | Controlled change management | Moderate |
| Risk | ISO reads as low-risk supplier | Major |
| Delivery | Predictability | Major |

### What it strengthens

- Cyber Security / vCISO — evidence, governance and audit discipline.
- MSP & Managed IT — controlled IT processes.
- HR & Employment Law — competence records.
- Sustainability / ESG — environmental controls.
- Bid Writing & Tenders — evidence mapping.
- OT / ICS Security — controlled engineering processes.
- Insurance Broking & Key Person Cover — risk registers and incident logs.

### Common questions about ISO standards

**What is ISO 9001:2026, and do I need to upgrade?**
ISO 9001:2026 is the new version of the quality standard, published on 16 September 2026. Certified organisations have until 30 September 2029 to transition, after which ISO 9001:2015 certificates expire or are withdrawn. The main changes are quality culture and ethical behaviour, separate requirements for risks and opportunities, and stronger change management. Plan the move at your next recertification rather than leaving it to the deadline.

**How long does ISO certification take?**
For most small and mid-sized manufacturers, ISO 9001 takes three to six months, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 four to six months, and ISO 27001 six to twelve months. Certificates then run on a three-year cycle with annual surveillance audits. Start at least six months before the tender you are aiming for.

**Which ISO standards do manufacturing buyers ask for?**
ISO 9001 is the one asked for most, because buyers use it as a risk filter for quality. ISO 14001 covers environmental management, ISO 45001 health and safety, and ISO 27001 information security where sensitive data is shared. Some OEMs and Tier-1s also expect sector standards, such as IATF 16949 in automotive or AS9100 in aerospace.

Sources: ISO 9001:2026 is live, the transition period has begun (LRQA) https://www.lrqa.com/en/latest-news/iso-9001-2026-live/

## People and Employment Law

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/hr-employment-law.html

**Proving your people are managed, protected and legally covered.**

Social value is now weighted heavily on manufacturing tenders, and HR evidence is where most of those marks live or die.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without current HR and employment documentation, a buyer assumes weak or absent EDI commitment, unaudited, higher-risk supply chain on modern slavery, IR35 and worker classification exposure, generic, unsubstantiated wellbeing claims and social value answers that won't survive scrutiny.
None of that may be true of you. It does not matter. In a tender, the assumption is what gets scored.

### The point most people miss

Most manufacturers have decent practice and no documentation. To an evaluator, undocumented good practice scores identically to having no practice at all.
This is not HR administration. It is operational risk control, and buyers score it that way.

### What it covers

#### EDI & Modern Slavery

Equality, diversity and inclusion policy plus a Modern Slavery statement backed by a real supply-chain audit.

#### Contracts & Classification

Employment contract review and IR35 worker classification that holds up to scrutiny.

#### Pay & Wellbeing

Real Living Wage accreditation and wellbeing programmes with substance behind them, not slogans.

#### Governance

TUPE readiness, right-to-work checks, grievance procedures and whistleblowing policy.

### What it looks like inside a manufacturer

- EDI policy exists, is current, and has a genuine action plan behind it.
- Modern Slavery statement is published and reflects an actual supply chain audit.
- Employment contracts are compliant and worker classification is defensible.
- Wellbeing initiatives are real and can be described with specifics, not slogans.
- TUPE processes are understood and ready before a contract requires them.
- Right-to-work checks are consistent and recorded.
- Grievance processes are documented and followed when used.
- HR documentation is reviewed annually, not written once and forgotten.

### Bid/Tender scoring impact

| Tender criterion | What this service contributes | Score effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ESG | EDI, wellbeing and pay policy score directly as social value | Major |
| Compliance | Modern Slavery statement is often a stated requirement | Major |
| Risk | Employment law exposure reads as operational risk | Moderate |
| Quality | Workforce governance supports process maturity claims | Moderate |
| Experience | Retention and wellbeing evidence strengthens capability | Moderate |

### What it strengthens

- Training and Skills — competence and development sit alongside workforce governance.
- Sustainability / ESG — social value scoring draws on both together.
- Web Design & Digital — Modern Slavery statement must be published.
- Commercial Solicitor — TUPE and employment risk in contract review.

### Common questions about HR and employment law

**Do I need a Modern Slavery statement?**
It is a legal requirement if your annual turnover is £36 million or more, under section 54 of the Modern Slavery Act 2015. Many buyers ask smaller suppliers for one anyway, or for a description of how they check their supply chain. Publish it on your website, have a director approve it, and update it every year.

**How do HR policies score in social value?**
They are where much of the social value score is evidenced. Central government gives social value at least a 10% weighting under PPN 002, and evaluators look for specifics: Real Living Wage, apprenticeships, an equality action plan with targets, and wellbeing support you can describe in detail. Good practice that is not written down scores the same as no practice at all.

**What HR documents should a manufacturer have before bidding?**
An equality, diversity and inclusion policy, a Modern Slavery statement, whistleblowing, grievance and disciplinary procedures, compliant employment contracts and consistent right-to-work records. If the contract could involve staff transferring, add a TUPE plan. Review the set once a year.

Sources: Publish an annual modern slavery statement (GOV.UK) https://www.gov.uk/guidance/publish-an-annual-modern-slavery-statement; PPN 002: Social value in central government contracts (GOV.UK) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html

## Sustainability and ESG

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/esg-sustainability.html

**Proving you operate ethically, sustainably and transparently.**

A Carbon Reduction Plan has moved from nice-to-have to a scored, sometimes mandatory, requirement. Manufacturers without one are increasingly locked out before the technical evaluation even starts.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without a published Carbon Reduction Plan, a buyer assumes no environmental measurement or accountability, social value answers are unsubstantiated, reputational risk from non-compliance with packaging or waste rules, a supplier behind the market on a now-standard requirement and weaker positioning against competitors who do publish one.
None of that may be true of you. It does not matter. In a tender, the assumption is what gets scored.

### The point most people miss

Most manufacturers think ESG is a paragraph on the website. Evaluators check whether the Carbon Reduction Plan is actually live, actually measured, and actually matches what the bid claims.
ESG is not reporting. It is evidence of how you actually behave.

### What it covers

#### Carbon Reduction

A published Carbon Reduction Plan and Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions measurement.

#### Environmental Controls

ISO 14001 alignment, waste management, energy efficiency and pollution prevention.

#### Compliance

Packaging EPR, WEEE and RoHS obligations met and documented.

#### Evidence for Tenders

Sustainability evidence packaged and published where evaluators can actually find it.

### What it looks like inside a manufacturer

- A Carbon Reduction Plan is live on the website, not sitting in a drawer.
- Emissions are calculated annually, not estimated in a hurry for the bid.
- Environmental targets are specific and time-bound, not aspirational language.
- Waste streams are separated, documented and recycling targets tracked.
- Energy usage is monitored and actually reducing.
- Environmental incidents are logged.
- ISO 14001 evidence backs up narrative claims.

### Bid/Tender scoring impact

| Tender criterion | What this service contributes | Score effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ESG | Direct, primary scoring category | Major |
| Compliance | Carbon Reduction Plan is a stated requirement on many contracts | Major |
| Risk | Environmental non-compliance is a reputational and legal risk | Major |
| Quality | ISO 14001 evidence supports process maturity claims | Moderate |
| Innovation | Net zero and efficiency initiatives support innovation answers | Moderate |

### What it strengthens

- ISO Consultant — ISO 14001 is the certified backbone of this evidence.
- HR & Employment Law — environmental and social value scoring sit together.
- Web Design & Digital — the Carbon Reduction Plan must be published and findable.
- Bid Writing & Tenders — social value answers draw directly on this evidence.

### Common questions about sustainability and ESG

**Do I need a Carbon Reduction Plan to win government contracts?**
Usually yes on central government contracts worth more than £5 million a year including VAT, and NHS rules reach further from 1 April 2027. Elsewhere it's down to the buyer, and many councils and prime contractors ask for one too.

**What must a Carbon Reduction Plan contain?**
Your Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, a defined subset of Scope 3 emissions, a commitment to reach net zero by 2050 for your UK operations, and the measures you are taking to get there. PPN 006 says it should be updated at least annually, published and clearly signposted on your UK website, and signed off by a director.

**What are Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions in plain English?**
Scope 1 is fuel you burn yourself, such as gas heating and company vehicles. Scope 2 is the electricity you buy. Scope 3 is everything else in your value chain. For a Carbon Reduction Plan, the Scope 3 part covers a defined set: upstream and downstream transport and distribution, waste from your operations, business travel and employee commuting.

Sources: PPN 006: Carbon Reduction Plans (GOV.UK) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-006-taking-account-of-carbon-reduction-plans-in-the-procurement-of-major-government-contracts/ppn-006-taking-account-of-carbon-reduction-plans-html

## Training and Skills

Source: https://yourbestsolution.co.uk/training-skills.html

**Proving your people are competent, not just present.**

A method statement that claims a trained, competent workforce is a claim. A training matrix with names, dates and expiry tracking is evidence, and evaluators are trained to spot the difference.

### What it costs you to leave alone

Without documented training and skills records, a buyer assumes unverified workforce competence behind method statement claims, key-person dependency with no succession plan, social value commitments with no substance behind them, inconsistent site safety competence and a workforce that can't be evidenced under audit.
None of that may be true of you. It does not matter. In a tender, the assumption is what gets scored.

### The point most people miss

Most manufacturers think competence is about running the course. It is about being able to produce the certificate, the date and the sign-off, six months later, without a scramble.
Training is an activity. Competence is a proof point. Auditors do not want to hear that you train your people. They want the matrix.

### What it covers

#### Competency Mapping

Training matrices that show who is qualified for what, and when it expires.

#### Accredited Training
